key_insight: APS-produced Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 coatings remained predominantly crystalline despite rapid cooling, while spray distance controlled a trade-off between hardness, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: A 90 mm spray distance offered the best reported balance of mechanical and electrochemical performance for these low-glass-forming-ability coatings.
method: Deposited Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 coatings by atmospheric plasma spraying at varying spray distances.
Characterized phase composition, lamellar microstructure, and porosity.
Evaluated hardness, wear resistance, and electrochemical behaviour.
evidence_signal: XRD detected α-Fe(Si) and Fe–Zr intermetallic phases with no detectable amorphous fraction; porosity ranged from 2.2% to 4.9%, and increasing spray distance improved hardness and wear resistance but reduced corrosion resistance.
watch_item: The 90 mm optimum applies to the investigated conditions; the abstract does not report uncertainty or sufficient process details to establish transferability.
paper_title: Phase Evolution and Structure–Property Relationships of Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 Coatings with Low GFA Produced by Atmospheric Plasma Spraying
